questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
digital growth credit = ka ze ni
digital secure banking = vo ni lu
growth secure savings = ze lu mi
credit banking savings = ka vo mi
digital growth savings = ze mi ni
What is the code for “growth”?
questions.explanation: Answer: ze. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: digital = ni, growth = ze, credit = ka, secure = lu, banking = vo, savings = mi.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 24 km north, turns left and walks 20 km, then turns left and walks 9 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 25. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 15 km along the initial direction and 20 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(15² + 20²) = 25 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 30 km north, turns right and walks 12 km, then turns right and walks 21 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 15. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 9 km along the initial direction and 12 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(9² + 12²) = 15 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 58 km west, turns left and walks 120 km, then turns left and walks 8 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 130. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 50 km along the initial direction and 120 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(50² + 120²) = 130 km.

questions.stem: B is the mother of E. A is the son of E. G is the father of E. How is A related to G?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. G is a parent of E, and A is E’s son. Hence A is G’s grandchild.

questions.stem: F is the brother of A. A is the mother of D. E is the father of F and A. How is F related to D?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. F is the brother of D’s mother A. Therefore F is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: F is the only daughter of C. C is the father of F. G is the son of F. H is the sister of C. How is C related to G?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. C is the father of F, and F is G’s mother. Thus C is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 60 candidates, a candidate is 11th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 47. New front rank = 11+3 = 14. Back rank = 60 − 14 + 1 = 47.

questions.stem: In a queue of 58 candidates, a candidate is 17th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 38. New front rank = 17+4 = 21. Back rank = 58 − 21 + 1 = 38.

questions.stem: An item costs ₹1050. It is marked above cost and sold at a 25% discount on marked price, earning 20% profit. Find the marked price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 1680. Selling price = 1050 × 120/100. Marked price = selling price ÷ 0.75 = 1680.

questions.stem: A can finish a job in 18 days and B in 27 days. They work together for 2 days, then B leaves. How many more days does A need? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 14.67. Use 54 work units. Rates: A = 3, B = 2 units/day. Remaining = 54 − 2×5. Divide by A’s rate 3.

questions.stem: A boat travels 247 km downstream and the same distance upstream. Its still-water speed is 16 km/h and stream speed is 3 km/h. Find the total time (hours).
A invests ₹16000 for 12 months. B invests ₹64000 for 7 months. Total profit is ₹68000. Find B’s share (₹).
questions.explanation: Answer: 47600. Capital-time ratio = 12 : 28. B’s share = total × 28/(40) = 47600.

questions.stem: What is the difference (₹) between compound interest and simple interest on ₹33000 at 5% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 82.5. For 2 years, CI − SI = P(r/100)² = 33000 × (5/100)².

questions.stem: A vessel contains 65 litres of milk and water in ratio 3:2. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 2:1?
questions.explanation: Answer: 13. Milk = 3V/5, water = 2V/5. Solve (3V/5 + x)/(2V/5) = 2; x = V/5 = 13.

questions.stem: The average of 26 numbers is 41. One number, 53, is replaced and the average rises by 5. What is the new number?
questions.explanation: Answer: 183. Total increases by 26 × 5. New number = 53 + 130.

questions.stem: A father is three times as old as his daughter. After 7 years, their combined age will be 86 years. Find the father’s present age.
questions.explanation: Answer: 54. Let daughter’s age be x. Father is 3x. 4x + 14 = 86; x = 18, so father = 54.
